qs.q: What is the primary mode of transmission for Trichomonas vaginalis?
o: Direct sexual contact with a partner
qs.e: Sexual transmission is the primary mode of infection for Trichomonas vaginalis since the parasite lacks a cyst stage and is an obligate parasite. Non-sexual transmission via fomites or during birth is much rarer.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the typical microscopic motility of Trichomonas vaginalis trophozoites?
o: Slow gliding movement along flat surfaces
Uniform forward swimming with one flagellum
qs.e: Under a microscope, T. vaginalis trophozoites exhibit a characteristic rapid, jerky, twitching movement powered by their four anterior flagella and an undulating membrane. This distinct motility helps differentiate them from other clinical specimens.

qs.q: What epithelial tissue type does Trichomonas vaginalis primarily infect in the human host?
qs.e: Trichomonas vaginalis primarily targets squamous epithelium rather than columnar epithelium, producing enzymes and acids that disrupt local metabolism. This infection site accounts for the common presentation of vaginitis and cervical erosion.

qs.q: Which clinical sign is classically associated with the localized tissue damage caused by Trichomonas vaginalis in females?
qs.e: The parasite causes inflammation, capillary dilation, and petechial hemorrhages that give the cervix a characteristic 'strawberry appearance'. This differs from ulcers or membranes seen in other sexually transmitted infections.

qs.q: What is considered the gold standard laboratory method for diagnosing Trichomonas vaginalis when initial microscopy is negative?
qs.e: Culture is regarded as the gold standard and the most sensitive method for detecting T. vaginalis when microscopic wet mounts are negative. Media such as CPLM and Diamond's medium are commonly utilized for this purpose.

qs.q: Which diagnostic modality yields the highest sensitivity and specificity for detecting Trichomonas vaginalis?
qs.e: Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests such as the Aptima assay are considered the most sensitive and specific diagnostic tests, boasting sensitivities around 97%. Wet mount microscopy, by contrast, has a significantly lower sensitivity of about 60%.

qs.q: What is the recommended first-line oral treatment regimen for an uncomplicated Trichomonas vaginalis infection?
qs.e: First-line treatment for trichomoniasis involves metronidazole, either as a 2 g single oral dose or 500 mg orally twice daily for 7 days. Tinidazole serves as an effective alternative option.

qs.q: Which cellular structure in Trichomonas vaginalis runs along the undulating membrane and is supported by a flexible rod?
qs.e: The organism possesses four anterior flagella for locomotion and a fifth flagellum that runs along the undulating membrane, supported by a flexible rod known as the costa. The axostyle is a separate rigid rod projecting posteriorly.

ai.summary: Trichomonas vaginalis is a flagellated protozoan that colonises the urogenital tract, producing frothy, malodorous discharge and a characteristic strawberry cervix. It is sexually transmitted, thrives in warm, anaerobic environments, and is often missed in low‑resource settings.

sections.p: A single‑cell, motile protozoan that infects the vaginal and urethral mucosa. It lacks a cyst stage, so transmission requires direct contact with trophozoites.
The parasite’s surface is covered with a glycocalyx that protects it from host defenses and facilitates attachment to epithelial cells.
Spread through vaginal intercourse; trophozoites survive in semen and vaginal fluid for up to 48 h. No environmental reservoir.
b: Sexual contact is the only route
No cyst stage, so no environmental persistence

t.b: Detects motile trophozoites; positive means active infection
Detects parasite antigen; positive confirms infection when microscopy unavailable

sections.p: Trichomoniasis presents with frothy, greenish discharge, pruritus, dysuria, and a strawberry cervix. In women, it increases risk of HIV acquisition and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
Microscopy of a fresh vaginal swab is the gold standard. Rapid antigen tests are useful where microscopy is unavailable. Culture is rarely used due to low yield.
b: Wet mount microscopy: look for motile trophozoites

t.b: Positive indicates infection; negative does not rule out if symptoms persist
Positive confirms infection; useful in low‑resource settings

sections.p: First‑line therapy is a single dose of a nitroimidazole. Treating partners and screening for co‑existing STIs are essential to prevent reinfection.
b: Nitroimidazole (e.g., metronidazole) chosen for efficacy and low resistance

t.b: Eradicates trophozoites; avoid in pregnancy or with alcohol

sections.p: Remember that trichomoniasis is the only common STI that is not detected by Gram stain. A strawberry cervix is pathognomonic.
b: Gram stain negative; wet mount positive

sections.p: Bacterial vaginosis and candidiasis also cause discharge but differ in colour, smell, and microscopic findings.
Wet mount can be falsely negative if the sample is old or if the parasite is in low numbers. Rapid tests may miss low‑density infections.

whenToSeekHelp: Severe pelvic pain, fever, or signs of sepsis
Pregnancy with severe symptoms or recurrent infection

faq.a: Yes, up to 70% of women have no symptoms, yet they can still transmit the parasite.
Yes, a single dose of a nitroimidazole usually cures the infection.
It is not a direct cause, but untreated infection can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease, which may impair fertility.
